Error monitoring cannot be switched off by a missing setting - CORRECTED AND RE-PROVEN 2026-08-28. The previous wording said the DSN is hard-coded in sentry.server.config.ts. That has been FALSE since cycle 52 (72a11bd), which moved it to process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN because the hardcoded DSN was sending CI's e2e traffic into the client's production Sentry project and exhausting its ingest quota. The CONCLUSION survives, for a different and now-measured reason: NEXT_PUBLIC_* is not a runtime lookup, it is substituted at `next build` and frozen, and .github/workflows/deploy-production.yml sets it as a LITERAL on the build step - deliberately not a secret or repo variable, either of which expands to an empty string when unset and would disable the SDK silently. Verified three ways rather than assumed: (1) the Azure App Service has NO Sentry setting - 38 app settings listed, none matching SENTRY - and does not need one; (2) built locally with the variable unset, a runtime process.env read REMAINS in the server chunk, but built with it set, the literal is baked into the server chunk, edge-instrumentation.js and the browser bundle with NO process.env read left anywhere in .next/server, so all three runtimes are inlined from the build environment; (3) the DSN is present in the main-app-*.js actually served by app-opensdoors-outreach-prod.azurewebsites.net. Guarded against drift by src/lib/monitoring/sentry-config-wiring.test.ts, which fails if the literal becomes a ${{ }} expression or moves off the build step - watched red by making exactly that change.
not_met: SENTRY EVENT ARRIVAL IS STILL UNOBSERVED. Wording corrected 2026-08-28: the DSN is not hard-coded, it is inlined at build time from a literal in deploy-production.yml, and the SDK is therefore initialised in production on all three runtimes - see the met[] entry for the measurements. What is proven is that the DSN REACHES the deployed code; what is still NOT proven is that an event LANDS. Nobody has looked at the Sentry dashboard and seen one arrive. 'Wired' is not 'receiving', and this project's signature defect is precisely the thing that is built, wired, reports success and never fires. This is the ONLY remaining gap between this grade and a 9, and it needs one look at a dashboard that was in a partial outage on 2026-08-27.

blockers.summary: Sentry was configured to collect prospect personal data, and the EMPTY dataCollection block was what turned it on. sentry.server.config.ts, sentry.edge.config.ts and src/instrumentation-client.ts each carried `dataCollection: {}` with every field commented out, which reads like the safe defaults were kept. It is the opposite: in @sentry/core 10.67.0, resolveDataCollectionOptions picks its base with `options.dataCollection != null ? DEFAULTS : legacyBridge(sendDefaultPii)`, and an empty object is not null - so SUPPLYING the block selects the PERMISSIVE defaults (userInfo, cookies, request and response headers, all four httpBodies, urlQueryParams, databaseQueryData and stackFrameVariables all on) and every commented-out line falls straight through to them. On this product that is prospect names, email addresses, the bodies of real outreach and real replies, prospect rows off the database, and the recipient address and rendered body sitting in local variables inside the send pipeline. Fixed by replacing the block in all three entry points with one shared EXPLICIT policy naming every field the SDK knows about. Deleting the block would have been safer than leaving it, but is not relied on: the SDK carries a TODO to remove the legacy bridge in v11, at which point an absent block would silently flip to the permissive defaults.
blockers.evidence: src/lib/monitoring/sentry-data-collection.ts, wired into all three entry points. Proven by two test files, both watched red before green in cycle 62. sentry-data-collection.test.ts drives the REAL installed resolver out of @sentry/core by absolute path (it is not re-exported from the package root) and asserts BOTH directions: the old `{}` shape resolves userInfo true, cookies true, four httpBodies, databaseQueryData true, stackFrameVariables true; ours resolves every one of those off. It also asserts our object's key set equals the resolver's whole output surface, so a field added by a future SDK version reds the build instead of inheriting `true`. sentry-config-wiring.test.ts proves the policy FIRES rather than merely existing: it imports the real sentry.server.config.ts, lets it call Sentry.init, and reads client.getDataCollectionOptions() back off the live client. Capability-to-fail demonstrated by restoring `dataCollection: {}` in the server config and watching the runtime assertion fail with `expected true to be false` - userInfo coming back TRUE off a live client in this application, which is the finding itself, observed rather than argued. Gates: lint clean, tsc --noEmit clean, 2900 tests in 293 files green. NOTE: two claims in this blocker's original text were already stale when written - the DSN is env-driven, not hard-coded (since cycle 52, 72a11bd), and tracesSampleRate is 0.1, not 1, in all three configs. Neither was touched by this fix.

blockers.evidence: Cycle 102, 2026-08-29, read-only against production via scripts/ops-bounce-path-audit.ts (workflow_dispatch runs 33257014566 and 33257443587, identical result twice). FIRST, THE SUMMARY'S OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG: 'nothing has sent since 3 July' is false - the real send range is 2026-05-20T12:24:54Z to 2026-08-26T13:07:09Z (1,361 sends ever, 0 new since the fix merged 2026-08-27). CENTRAL FINDING: 11 OutboundEmail rows carry status=BOUNCED, all via the mailbox NDR channel (bounceCategory ndr:subject,5xx), none via the ESP webhook. Every row's updatedAt (2026-08-28T19:06:xx, the actual database write time) is AFTER the fix merged, which is the only fact that can attribute the write to this code - the rows' own bouncedAt event times (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-03) predate the fix and cannot be used for that, exactly the trap PR #386 fixed the probe against. So these are historical NDRs sitting in opensdoors.co.uk mailboxes that record-bounce.ts, running live in production with the flag on, picked up and stamped for the first time - a real bounce, moving the reported rate off 0%, observed rather than argued. Confirmed MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED=true directly in the production App Service config (az webapp config appsettings list, not assumed from a default). Checked the ESP webhook side named in the row: POST https://app-opensdoors-outreach-prod.azurewebsites.net/api/webhooks/resend returns HTTP 503, and neither RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET nor RESEND_API_KEY exists in production app settings - the route is deployed and reachable but genuinely unconfigured. blockers.evidence: Cycle 100, 2026-08-29. Measured BEFORE changing anything, as the queue row demanded: a new merge-blocking spec (e2e/mobile-walk.spec.ts) drives a real Chromium page at a 375x667 phone viewport (iPhone SE - the smallest phone still in real use) through the five journeys OpensDoors staff actually use between client sites - client list, one client's overview, the mailboxes tab, the setup-help page, and the outreach send-preparation screen carrying the four-at-a-time corporate send gate (src/lib/outreach/manual-send-window.ts) - and asserts, per screen: no horizontal page overflow, no rendered text under 12px, no table wider than the viewport without its own horizontal scroller, and no interactive control smaller than 24px (WCAG 2.5.8). RED FIRST, and it found four real defects, not zero: (1) client-list's client-logo monogram tile rendered its initials at 11px (src/components/clients/client-logo.tsx - fontSize formula had no floor); (2) client-overview's Operational Snapshot card labels/hints used a literal text-[11px] (src/components/clients/client-operational-snapshot.tsx); (3) the mailboxes table's action-button column wrapped 'Set primary / Reconnect / Disconnect / Remove / Edit' onto two lines inside its own horizontal scroller, which inflated EVERY row to ~97px and left a misleading block of blank space under the still-visible Mailbox/Provider columns - fixed by letting that button group scroll instead of wrap (src/components/clients/client-mailbox-identities-panel.tsx), which shrank the whole page by ~264px with nothing removed; (4) setup-help's SPF and DMARC DNS records - the exact strings a customer's IT department is asked to copy-paste - used break-all inside a cramped label+value+button row, so v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all rendered chopped mid-word ('spf.pro' / 'tection.outlook.com'); fixed by giving the record its own full-width line with break-words (src/components/clients/client-deliverability-help.tsx), which now wraps at the space before -all instead of mid-token. A methodology bug was found and fixed in the SAME cycle before it produced a false finding: Chromium keeps a cached, non-zero getBoundingClientRect for a closed <details> panel's children (so re-expanding is instant), which read six owner-only diagnostic strings as an 11px violation even though nothing was painted; Element.checkVisibility() is the one API that accounts for this and was added as a gate on every check, verified against the panel both ways (open vs Playwright's checkVisibility() reporting false while collapsed). RE-WALKED to prove it: all 5 journeys pass clean after the four fixes. Full gates on the same commit: lint 0, tsc --noEmit 0, 3644/3644 unit tests, and the FULL Playwright suite (not just the new spec) at 91/92 (1 pre-existing skip, unrelated) - proving the shared-component changes (ClientLogo, the mailboxes table, the operational snapshot) did not regress screen-walk, mailboxes-table-first or any other existing spec. NOT DONE, named rather than hidden: the send-preparation screen's POPULATED state - the actual four-at-a-time batch/cooldown UI - was not exercised, because the e2e fixture client has no active sequence and the panel renders its clean empty state instead ('No sequences yet'); seeding a launchable sequence was judged out of scope for a single cycle (it touches ContactList/Template/Sequence/Enrollment rows in a shared seed file seven other specs depend on) and is left as a named follow-up rather than claimed. Also only one viewport was measured (375x667); a second breakpoint (e.g. 390x844) was not run. Closing this on the strength of five real, reproducible fixes with before/after proof and full-suite regression coverage - not on the strength of a guess.

blockers.summary: Art.28 data-processing agreements. Researched 2026-08-27 from each vendor's published DPA: RESEND binds automatically via its Terms of Service, including EU and UK SCCs (resend.com/legal/dpa) - nothing to do. ROCKETREACH forms part of its Terms of Service with no separate signature (rocketreach.co/dpa), though note the role split - it is an INDEPENDENT CONTROLLER for the prospect records it sells and a processor only for data we supply. SENTRY is the one real action and it is self-serve: Greg accepts it under Legal & Compliance in the Sentry org settings. Attempted 2026-08-27 at approximately 10:00 UTC and blocked by a Sentry platform outage, not by inaction. Record the who-and-when Sentry's page shows afterwards, not a bare assertion.
blockers.evidence: All three Art.28 processor agreements are now in place, each with its own instrument named. SENTRY: Data Processing Amendment VERSION 5.1.0 SIGNED 28 AUGUST 2026, accepted by Greg Visser in the Sentry organisation `bidlowai` (org id 4511767741071360) and shown with a green tick at https://bidlowai.sentry.io/settings/legal/ - observed on screen at the moment of signing, not reported. Sentry's DPA is not automatic: v5.1.0 binds only 'the party that electronically accepts or otherwise agrees or opts-in', which is why this one needed a human. Also confirmed on that page: the organisation's Data Storage Region is EUROPEAN UNION, and 'Use of aggregated identifying data' is OFF. RESEND: no signature required - the DPA is incorporated into the Terms of Service and 'shall become legally binding upon Customer entering into the Agreement', with EU and UK SCCs included and the parties 'deemed to have signed the EU SCCs' (resend.com/legal/dpa, last updated 31 December 2025). ROCKETREACH: no signature required - the DPA 'forms part of the RocketReach Terms of Service'; SCCs and UK SCCs are the transfer instrument. NOTE the role split, which matters for this product: both parties are INDEPENDENT CONTROLLERS for RocketReach's own prospect data, and RocketReach is a processor only for data we supply. Their page publishes no effective date - recorded as a gap rather than invented. NOT LEGAL ADVICE: this records what each vendor publishes and what was signed, not a legal opinion.

blockers.summary: Six AI features shipped 28-29 August 2026 (row 80) call Anthropic's Messages API (src/server/ai/anthropic-messages.ts). One of them, classify-inbound-reply.ts, sends a real prospect's own reply text - subject plus up to 2,000 characters of body, verbatim - to Anthropic in order to label it. No Art.28 DPA exists for Anthropic; CR-05 covered only Sentry, Resend and RocketReach. Found while re-measuring dimension 8 for row 93, not while looking for it.
blockers.evidence: Measured 2026-08-30, cycle 122. NOT currently firing: `az webapp config appsettings list` against the live production App Service (app-opensdoors-outreach-prod, rg-opensdoors-outreach-prod) lists all 38 real app settings and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not among them; src/server/ai/metered-call.ts, which all six AI features route through exclusively, refuses with `no_api_key` before any network call when the key is absent - confirmed by reading the gate, not by trusting it. The other five AI features (review-campaign, draft-sequence, advise-send-times, advise-title-messages, explain-rep-performance) were checked and do not carry a prospect's name, address or message body - explain-rep-performance sends the client's OWN mailbox identity, the rest send aggregated statistics or the client's own template copy. The gap is that the ONLY thing standing between 'inert' and 'a real prospect reply reaching an uncovered third party' is whether an environment variable happens to be set - there is no code-level check that a DPA exists before the key is allowed to work. Needs a decision: either accept an Art.28 DPA with Anthropic before ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is ever set in production, or add a compliance gate (mirroring the pattern in src/lib/monitoring/sentry-data-collection.ts) that refuses the classify-inbound-reply call independently of whether a key is present until a DPA-accepted flag is set. Recording it now so it is not rediscovered as a live incident later, the way CR-06 nearly was.
